atom_statement: Identify the authors of a dataset.
need_statement: Users can know the creator of a dataset.
rationale_A: The creator of a dataset is its author, a close synonym in this context.
rationale_B: Creator and author of a dataset are close synonyms, so this is the same information item for the same resource.

atom_statement: Describe the lineage of a dataset.
need_statement: Users can know what typed relationships connect the resource to related objects for a resource.
rationale_A: Typed relationships can record derivation links that are part of lineage, but the need covers relationships in general rather than a lineage description.
rationale_B: Typed relations such as derivation links express part of a lineage, but the need is a general relation mechanism for any resource.

atom_statement: Describe the lineage of a dataset.
need_statement: Users can know narrative descriptions that explain the resource, its methods or technical information for a dataset.
rationale_A: Methods descriptions overlap with lineage, but the need also covers abstracts and technical information and does not target lineage as such.
rationale_B: A methods narrative overlaps a lineage description, but the need covers descriptions in general (abstract, methods, technical information) rather than lineage as such.

atom_statement: Link a dataset to scientific publications about it.
need_statement: Users can know what typed relationships connect the resource to related objects for a resource.
rationale_A: Typed relationships to related objects include a link from a dataset to publications about it, among other relations.
rationale_B: Typed relationships from a resource to related objects include links from a dataset to publications about it, among other relations.

atom_statement: Link a dataset to its input data (the data used to create it).
need_statement: Users can know what typed relationships connect the resource to related objects for a resource.
rationale_A: Typed relationships to related objects include a link from a dataset to its input data, among other relations.
rationale_B: Typed relationships to related objects include a link from a dataset to the data it was derived from, among other relations.

atom_statement: Use persistent identifiers for dataset authors and input data, so datasets can be reliably filtered and linked by them.
need_statement: Users can know the unique identifier of the dataset.
rationale_A: Asks for a dataset's own unique identifier, not persistent identifiers for its authors and input data used for filtering and linking.
adjudication: unrelated: The need concerns the dataset's own identifier, not persistent identifiers for its authors or input data used for filtering and linking; sharing the notion of an identifier is not a relation by itself.

atom_statement: Use persistent identifiers for dataset authors and input data, so datasets can be reliably filtered and linked by them.
need_statement: Users can know the identifier (URI) of the catalog's publisher.
rationale_A: Asks for an agent identifier (URI), but for the catalogue's publisher rather than dataset authors, without persistence or the filtering/linking purpose.
adjudication: unrelated: The need concerns the catalogue publisher's URI, a different agent role on a different resource with no persistence or filtering/linking purpose, so only the generic notion of an identifier is shared.

atom_statement: Distinguish primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.
need_statement: Users can know identifiers other than the primary DOI together with their identifier types for a dataset.
rationale_A: Separates a dataset's alternative identifiers from its primary DOI, but covers only the alternative side and adds identifier types.
rationale_B: It separates alternative identifiers from the primary DOI, but it fixes the primary identifier to a DOI and adds identifier types.

atom_statement: Use a DOI as the dataset identifier when generating DataCite citations.
need_statement: Users can know identifiers other than the primary DOI together with their identifier types for a dataset.
rationale_A: Assumes a primary DOI for the dataset but asks for its other identifiers and their types, with no DataCite citation context.
rationale_B: It presupposes that the dataset's primary identifier is a DOI, but it asks for the other identifiers and their types and has no DataCite-citation condition.

atom_statement: Use a DOI as the dataset identifier when generating DataCite citations.
need_statement: Users can know the unique identifier of the dataset.
rationale_A: Asks for the dataset identifier without requiring it to be a DOI or the DataCite citation context.
adjudication: partial: Both concern the dataset's identifier, but the need neither requires a DOI nor is tied to DataCite citations, so they overlap without either containing the other.

atom_statement: Qualify each identifier with its scheme or type.
need_statement: Users can know identifiers other than the primary DOI together with their identifier types for a dataset.
rationale_A: Covers identifier types only for a dataset's alternative identifiers other than the primary DOI.
rationale_B: Identifier types for a dataset's non-primary identifiers are a special case of qualifying each identifier with its type.

atom_statement: Use a minimal, consistent set of unambiguous agent roles beyond publisher and contact point.
need_statement: Users can know which role types (e.g., contact, curation) are associated with contributors for a dataset.
rationale_A: Typed contributor roles overlap with additional agent roles, but include contact roles and do not ask for a minimal unambiguous role set.
rationale_B: Typed contributor roles such as curation go beyond publisher and contact point, but the need also includes contact roles and does not ask for a minimal, unambiguous role set.

atom_statement: Use a minimal, consistent set of unambiguous agent roles beyond publisher and contact point.
need_statement: Users can know which curation role types are associated with contributors for a dataset.
rationale_A: Curation role types are one kind of additional agent role, without a minimal, consistent role set.
rationale_B: Curation roles are one kind of agent role beyond publisher and contact point, but the need does not ask for a minimal, consistent role set.

atom_statement: Use a minimal, consistent set of unambiguous agent roles beyond publisher and contact point.
need_statement: Users can know which contact role types are associated with contributors for a dataset.
rationale_A: Contact role types for contributors are typed agent roles, but sit in the contact-point area and do not address a minimal unambiguous set.
rationale_B: Same role-typing item, but for contact roles, which the atom places outside its scope, and without a minimal role set.

atom_statement: Indicate when a distribution points to a service or API rather than directly to the data.
need_statement: Users can know the accepted interfaces through which the JRC data can be accessed.
rationale_A: Knowing the interfaces through which data are accessed overlaps with flagging service/API access, but the need does not mark individual distributions.
rationale_B: Knowing the interfaces through which data are accessed overlaps flagging service/API access, but it is a general statement about JRC data, not a per-distribution indication.

atom_statement: Describe the API or service interface, with the query parameters needed to select data, so software agents can use it directly.
need_statement: Users can know the accepted interfaces through which the JRC data can be accessed.
rationale_A: Asks to know the accepted access interfaces, not a description with query parameters for direct use by software agents.
rationale_B: Knowing which interfaces give access overlaps describing the API, but the need asks for no interface description or query parameters and does not target software agents.

atom_statement: Describe provenance in enough detail to support reproducibility and to track how data are used.
need_statement: Users can know what typed relationships connect the resource to related objects for a resource.
rationale_A: Typed relationships can record derivation and usage links, but the need is not a detailed provenance description for reproducibility.
rationale_B: Typed relations such as derivation or citation links carry some provenance and usage information, but the need is a general relation mechanism without reproducibility-level detail.

atom_statement: Describe provenance in enough detail to support reproducibility and to track how data are used.
need_statement: Users can know narrative descriptions that explain the resource, its methods or technical information for a dataset.
rationale_A: Methods descriptions support reproducibility, but the need is not a provenance description and does not address usage tracking.
rationale_B: A methods narrative is part of provenance and helps reproducibility, but the need does not ask for detailed provenance or usage tracking.

atom_statement: Describe the dimensions that identify observations in a statistical dataset (e.g. time, sex, age, region), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can judge that dimension values within a dataset are unambiguously defined, when evaluating the dataset's metadata.
rationale_A: Concerns the dataset metadata defining dimension values unambiguously, which overlaps with but is not the same as describing the dimensions.
rationale_B: Dataset metadata letting users judge that dimension values are unambiguously defined overlaps on describing dimensions but focuses on value definitions.

atom_statement: Describe the dimensions that identify observations in a statistical dataset (e.g. time, sex, age, region), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can know what dimensions (time period, region, sex) are available for query and their presentational order.
rationale_A: Asks for the dataset's dimensions (time period, region, sex) plus their presentational order, with no format-independence condition.
rationale_B: Asks which dimensions (time period, region, sex) are available plus their presentational order, without the format-independence condition.

atom_statement: Describe the dimensions that identify observations in a statistical dataset (e.g. time, sex, age, region), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can know the values of each dimension required to locate an observation for a Dataset observation.
rationale_A: Asks for each observation's values of its identifying dimensions, observation-level data rather than a dataset-level description of the dimensions.
rationale_B: Values of each identifying dimension for an individual observation: observation level rather than a dataset-level description of the dimensions.

atom_statement: Describe the dimensions that identify observations in a statistical dataset (e.g. time, sex, age, region), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can know which dimensions are required for each qb:Observation in a qb:DataSet.
rationale_A: Asks which dimensions each observation needs, but only for a Data Cube qb:DataSet rather than a format-independent dataset description.
rationale_B: Which dimensions each Data Cube observation must have overlaps on the dataset's dimensions but is framed as Data Cube requiredness, not a format-independent description.

atom_statement: Describe the attributes needed to qualify and interpret observed values (e.g. units of measure, scaling factors, observation status), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Publishers can indicate whether an attribute is required for every observation; otherwise the attribute is optional.
rationale_A: Concerns flagging attributes as required or optional for observations, an aspect of attribute description rather than the attributes themselves.
rationale_B: Stating whether an attribute is required for every observation covers one aspect of attributes in Data Cube terms, not their format-independent description.

atom_statement: Describe the attributes needed to qualify and interpret observed values (e.g. units of measure, scaling factors, observation status), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can know the units (years) of the measured values for each observation.
rationale_A: Covers only the unit-of-measure attribute, as per-observation values.
rationale_B: Unit of each observation's value: one attribute at observation level rather than a format-independent description of the dataset's attributes.

atom_statement: Describe the attributes needed to qualify and interpret observed values (e.g. units of measure, scaling factors, observation status), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can know that component properties such as unit of measure can be attached at the dataset level to avoid redundancy.
rationale_B: Data Cube guidance that attributes such as unit of measure can be attached at dataset level overlaps on dataset-level attributes but is modelling advice.
adjudication: partial: Shares attributes such as unit of measure that qualify observed values but concerns attaching them at dataset level to avoid redundancy, not describing them the same way across formats.

atom_statement: Describe the attributes needed to qualify and interpret observed values (e.g. units of measure, scaling factors, observation status), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can find the unit of measurement and whether a value is measured or estimated for an Observation.
rationale_A: Covers two of the attributes (unit, measured/estimated status) as per-observation values, not a format-independent description of the dataset's attributes.
rationale_B: Unit and measured/estimated status of a single observation: two of the example attributes, at observation level, without the format-independent dataset description.

atom_statement: Describe the attributes needed to qualify and interpret observed values (e.g. units of measure, scaling factors, observation status), the same way whatever the distribution format.
need_statement: Users can know which attributes are marked as required for qb:Observations.
rationale_A: Asks which attributes are required for qb:Observations, a Data Cube-specific subset of the attributes.
rationale_B: Which attributes are required for qb:Observations identifies a subset of attributes in Data Cube terms, not a format-independent description.

atom_statement: State the unit of measurement of the observations in a dataset.
need_statement: Users can know the units (years) of the measured values for each observation.
rationale_A: Asks for the unit of measurement of the observed values (years is only an example).
rationale_B: Knowing the unit of each observation's measured value is stating the unit of measurement of the observations.

atom_statement: State the unit of measurement of the observations in a dataset.
need_statement: Users can know that component properties such as unit of measure can be attached at the dataset level to avoid redundancy.
rationale_A: Says unit of measure can be attached once at dataset level, a modelling option overlapping with stating the dataset's unit.
rationale_B: Says unit of measure can be attached at dataset level (where to state it), not the unit itself.

atom_statement: State the unit of measurement of the observations in a dataset.
need_statement: Users can find the unit of measurement and whether a value is measured or estimated for an Observation.
rationale_A: Asks for the unit of measurement of an observation plus whether its value is measured or estimated.
rationale_B: Asks for the unit of measurement of an observation plus whether its value is measured or estimated.

atom_statement: State the start of the period a time series covers.
need_statement: Users can know the temporal coverage of a dataset.
rationale_A: Temporal coverage of any dataset includes the start (and end) of the covered period.
rationale_B: Temporal coverage of any dataset includes the start of the period a time series covers, plus its end.

atom_statement: State the end of the period a time series covers.
need_statement: Users can know the temporal coverage of a dataset.
rationale_A: Temporal coverage of any dataset includes the end (and start) of the covered period.
rationale_B: Temporal coverage of any dataset includes the end of the period a time series covers, plus its start.

atom_statement: Classify statistical datasets by EU data theme, mapping Eurostat's own themes onto it.
need_statement: Users can know core metadata of a dataset such as title, description, issued date, modified date, subject.
rationale_A: Lists a dataset's subject among core metadata; overlaps only with the classification aspect, without EU data theme or mapping.
rationale_B: Subject is one of several core dataset fields; topical classification overlaps but EU data themes and the Eurostat mapping are absent.

atom_statement: Classify statistical datasets by EU data theme, mapping Eurostat's own themes onto it.
need_statement: Users can know that dataset themes are represented by skos:Concepts organized in a skos:ConceptScheme, linked via dcat:themeTaxonomy.
rationale_A: Concerns representing dataset themes as concepts of a declared theme taxonomy, not classifying by EU data theme with a Eurostat mapping.
rationale_B: How dataset themes come from a SKOS concept scheme via a theme taxonomy, without EU data themes or the Eurostat mapping.

atom_statement: Classify statistical datasets by EU data theme, mapping Eurostat's own themes onto it.
need_statement: Users can know the thematic classification (SKOS concept) of a dataset.
rationale_A: Asks for a dataset's thematic classification in general, without the EU data theme vocabulary or the Eurostat theme mapping.
rationale_B: Thematic classification of a dataset with any SKOS concept, without the EU data theme vocabulary or the mapping of Eurostat themes.

atom_statement: Link an RDF distribution to the data structure definition it follows.
need_statement: Users can judge that each dataset has exactly one associated data structure definition.
rationale_A: Concerns a dataset's single associated data structure definition rather than linking an RDF distribution to the DSD it follows.
rationale_B: Association of a (Data Cube) dataset with exactly one data structure definition: the same link for a different resource, as an integrity check.

atom_statement: Record publication and modification times to the time of day when data are published more than once a day.
need_statement: Users can know core metadata of a dataset such as title, description, issued date, modified date, subject.
rationale_A: Lists a dataset's issued and modified dates among other core metadata, without the time-of-day precision for multiple daily publication.
rationale_B: Issued and modified dates of a dataset among other core fields, without time-of-day precision or the multiple-daily-publication condition.
adjudication: partial: Lists a dataset's issued and modified dates among other fields but does not ask for the time-of-day precision the atom requires, so neither contains the other.

atom_statement: Record publication and modification times to the time of day when data are published more than once a day.
need_statement: Users can know the semantics of date properties such as release date, modification date, and listing date for datasets and catalog records.
rationale_A: Concerns the meaning of dataset release and modification dates, not recording them to the time of day.
adjudication: unrelated: Asks for the meaning of date properties, a different information item from recording publication and modification times to the time of day; only the terms are shared.

atom_statement: Record publication and modification times to the time of day when data are published more than once a day.
need_statement: Users can know release date (dct:issued) for a Catalog
rationale_A: Release date of a catalogue rather than of datasets, without time-of-day precision.
adjudication: partial: Same information item (release date) but for a catalogue rather than datasets, and without the time-of-day precision or the multiple-daily-publication condition.

atom_statement: Record publication and modification times to the time of day when data are published more than once a day.
need_statement: Users can know update/modification date (dct:modified) for a Catalog
rationale_A: Modification date of a catalogue rather than of datasets, without time-of-day precision.
adjudication: partial: Same information item (modification date) but for a catalogue rather than datasets, and without the time-of-day precision or the multiple-daily-publication condition.
